title: Design partner beta: Private upgrade + rollback (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped)
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
description:
Goal
Ship a structured beta of the new Redwood Private upgrade + rollback workflow with 2 design partners:
1) Regulated VPC environment
2) On-prem / air-gapped environment

This ticket tracks milestones, partner feedback, and GA readiness signals (success metrics + support readiness).

Design partners (target)
- Cascade Financial Group (VPC private deployment): strict maintenance windows, rollback expectations, wants clear change-management + evidence.
- Northstar Health Systems (on-prem/air-gapped): offline bundles + artifact mirror constraints, stronger audit log + backup encryption expectations.

Scope of beta
- N-1 -> N upgrade path only (default).
- Installer-driven upgrade plan generation + preflight checks + backup orchestration + rollback command.
- Helm ordering and CP/DP readiness gates (control plane before data plane).
- Audit log events for upgrade lifecycle.

Out of scope
- Multi-hop automation (N-3 -> N).
- Fully automatic resolution for historical migration edge cases (must have explicit operator guidance when manual intervention is required).

Success criteria (beta)
- 2 successful upgrades to target release (TBD by Release Eng) with documented evidence.
- 1 rollback drill per partner (either full rollback or partial rollback simulation) without data loss / inconsistent state.
- Prechecks catch at least one real issue per partner environment (storage headroom, RBAC/OIDC reachability, artifact availability, etc.) with actionable remediation.
- Support can triage using support bundle + upgrade plan artifact without engineering involvement for "known" failure classes.

Artifacts / references
- Confluence: Private upgrade/rollback overview; prechecks spec; backup/restore strategy; rollback semantics; on-prem bundle format; operator runbook; change-management policy.
- GitHub PRs (tracking): installer plan generator; preflight framework; backup orchestrator; rollback command; air-gapped bundle verification; helm CP/DP phases; terraform version pinning + upgrade windows; audit log events; migration guardrails.

Owner notes
We should treat the beta as a release train milestone, not an ad-hoc upgrade. Each partner must have: (a) pre-beta readiness review, (b) scheduled maintenance window, (c) named Redwood on-call coverage plan, (d) rollback decision tree agreed up front.

---
Milestone plan

Milestone 0: Confirm partner constraints + scope lock (by 2025-05-20)
- Confirm current versions (N-1 baseline) and cluster facts (K8s version, storage backend, DB deployment) for each partner.
- Confirm upgrade window length and acceptable downtime.
- Confirm who owns backups, where keys live (KMS/HSM), and retention policy.

Milestone 1: Beta readiness review (by 2025-06-07)
- Installer version selected + pinned (Terraform or installer config).
- Precheck set enabled (blocking vs warning aligned with policy).
- Backup strategy confirmed and tested in staging-like environment.
- Rollback entry points understood (including schema migration constraints).
- Support readiness: escalation path + template response ready.

Milestone 2: Execute upgrade (by 2025-06-21)
- Run upgrade plan generation.
- Run prechecks; remediate any blockers.
- Execute upgrade.
- Verify health: API latency/5xx, control plane connectivity, model serving, background jobs, metrics.

Milestone 3: Rollback drill (by 2025-06-24)
- Execute planned rollback drill (ideally same week, while context is fresh).
- Collect evidence: state machine log, audit log entries, post-rollback verification.

Milestone 4: Beta closeout + GA recommendation (by 2025-06-28)
- Capture feedback + gaps.
- Decide GA blockers vs follow-ups.
- Update PM-812 GA requirements checklist.

---
Partner execution trackers

A) Cascade Financial Group (VPC)
- Target window (tentative): 2025-06-18 02:00–04:00 local
- Key risks: OIDC reachability during maintenance; strict rollback guarantee expectations; wants evidence for change mgmt approvals.
- Pre-beta checklist
  - [ ] Confirm current Private version + control plane connectivity expectations
  - [ ] Confirm DB hosting mode (managed vs in-cluster) and snapshot mechanism
  - [ ] Confirm artifact source (hosted registry vs mirror)
  - [ ] Confirm audit log export path (SIEM) and retention
- Upgrade day checklist
  - [ ] Generate plan; attach plan summary to support bundle
  - [ ] Prechecks pass (or warnings explicitly approved)
  - [ ] Backup complete + verification step recorded
  - [ ] Upgrade control plane phase complete + readiness gate
  - [ ] Upgrade data plane phase complete
  - [ ] Post-check: error rates normal; dashboards annotated with upgrade window
- Rollback drill
  - [ ] Choose failure injection (safe): simulate partial DP rollout OR invoke rollback after CP phase
  - [ ] Verify rollback hooks complete; ensure schema state consistent

B) Northstar Health Systems (On-prem / air-gapped)
- Target window (tentative): 2025-06-20 21:00–23:00 local
- Key risks: offline bundle verification (checksum/signature); storage backend variability; limited remote access; needs very explicit operator UX.
- Pre-beta checklist
  - [ ] Validate offline bundle creation flow + manifest checks
  - [ ] Confirm artifact mirror endpoints and certificate chain
  - [ ] Confirm snapshot approach (CSI vs logical dump) and encryption at rest
  - [ ] Confirm runbook steps are actionable without Redwood access to cluster
- Upgrade day checklist
  - [ ] Bundle verified offline (checksums/signatures)
  - [ ] Prechecks pass; capture full output for evidence
  - [ ] Backup complete (and keys verified)
  - [ ] Upgrade proceeds with clear progress reporting
  - [ ] Post-check: control plane reaches ready; data plane serving validated
- Rollback drill
  - [ ] Rollback performed with offline artifacts available
  - [ ] Verify restore step + health checks; no orphaned resources

---
GA readiness checklist (draft; feed into PM-812)
- Product
  - [ ] Supported upgrade path policy documented (N-1 -> N)
  - [ ] "Blocking" prechecks list stable + matches change-management policy
  - [ ] Rollback contract documented (including limitations around migrations)
- Engineering
  - [ ] Installer: plan artifact persisted + included in support bundle
  - [ ] Audit log events emitted: start/stop, precheck pass/fail, backup complete, rollback invoked, rollback complete
  - [ ] Helm ordering: CP/DP phases + timeouts are tuned
  - [ ] Terraform: version pinning + upgrade window variables documented
- Ops / Support
  - [ ] Operator runbook reviewed by SRE + Support (clear decision tree: rollback vs manual fix)
  - [ ] On-call playbook updated (upgrade alerts, dashboard annotation)
  - [ ] Known failure classes and remediation snippets published internally

---
Metrics to track (beta)
- Upgrade success rate (per environment)
- Precheck failure categories and time-to-remediate
- Backup time and restore verification time
- Migration duration + lock timeouts observed
- Rollback frequency and success rate
- Support ticket volume + time-to-triage for upgrade-related issues

Risks / open questions
- If partner is >N-1, do we enforce "stop" vs allow with warnings + sign-off? Current policy recommendation: stop (unless explicit exception from SRE + Release Eng).
- Rollback expectations when a schema migration is non-reversible: we need to ensure messaging is explicit and the rollback command does the safest action (e.g., restore from backup) rather than "best effort".
- Air-gapped environment: need to confirm signature verification keys distribution and rotation story.

Next actions (this week)
- Schedule readiness review calls w/ both partners and internal stakeholders (Release Eng + SRE + Security).
- Confirm target release versions and freeze plan for beta window.
- Publish beta comms template to partners (maintenance window, expected downtime, how to capture logs, rollback policy).
